thread.title: Saudi Aramco IPO Seen Likely Delayed Until 2019: Khalid al-Falih

author: GILLIAN RICH
title: Saudi Aramco IPO Seen Likely Delayed Until 2019: Khalid al-Falih
text:
The long-awaited Saudi Aramco initial public offering will "most likely" happen next year, but it depends on the oil market, said Saudi Arabia's energy minster as he dropped hints that sank the oil market Friday.
X
The state-run oil company, which is the world's largest oil producer and one of its biggest companies by revenue, was supposed to list a 5% stake on an exchange this year and generate capital for the country's economic reforms.
Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has estimated Aramco's valuation at $2 trillion, meaning the IPO could yield proceeds of $100 billion and dwarf Alibaba's ( BABA ) $25 billion haul as the biggest-ever IPO.
But some analysts say the figure is closer to $1 trillion. But even then, that would be bigger than Apple ( AAPL ) and Amazon.com ( AMZN ), as they close in on the $1 trillion mark, and nearly three times the valuation of oil giant Exxon Mobil ( XOM ).

In March, sources told the Financial Times that it would likely to be pushed back to next year or possibly later. Later that month, sources told the Wall Street Journal that Aramco would hold off on an international IPO and instead list on a domestic exchange next year.
Then on Friday, Saudi Energy Minister and Aramco Chairman Khalid al-Falih told reporters "most likely it will be in 2019, but we will not know until the announcement has been made. All I could say is stay tuned."
In March, he downplayed the importance of the IPO's timing , saying "between December 31 (2018) and January 1 (2019) there is no value lost for the kingdom."
Several reasons have come up for the delay. Previously, it was due to low oil prices, which would've weighed on proceeds from Aramco's offering. But until prices fell this week, they were at the highest levels since 2014.
Other factors include Riyadh's desire to seek a higher valuation for Aramco before going public as well as deciding where to list shares. The kingdom had wanted a listing on major exchanges in New York or London but has balked at the disclosures that would've been required.
On Friday, Falih attributed a delay to the market, in which he plays a key role as the de facto leader of OPEC.
"The timing I think will depend on the readiness of the market, rather than the readiness of the company or the readiness of Saudi Arabia," he said.
Falih wielded his market influence, telling reporters that oil production may rise later this year as Saudi Arabia and Russia debate how much to boost crude output over worries that higher oil prices could stifle global demand.
U.S. crude tumbled 4.5% to settle at $67.56 a barrel and lost 5.3% for the week. Brent fell 3.4%, to $76.12 per barrel and lost 3% for the week.
Still, Saudi Arabia won't want oil prices to fall too far as it looks to get a good price for Aramco's IPO.
"We are ready. The company essentially has ticked all the boxes," al-Falih said. "We're simply waiting for a market readiness for the IPO."
